elements.element: Customer is not prohibited from participating in competing or similar projects or otherwise subject to a non-compete-style exclusivity restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 prohibits the Company for twelve months from participating in any Internet project similar to the Site with respect to Deerskin Products.

elements.element: Vendor has no sole-supplier or equivalent exclusive-provider right that binds Customer regarding Customer's products or brand.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 continues to give HDI the exclusive right to use the “Deerskin” brand for a self-contained consumer website, thereby retaining an exclusive-provider arrangement.

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction is expressly limited to “Deerskin Products”; the prior expansion to substantially similar products and named competitors' products was removed.

elements.element: The exclusivity obligation lasts no longer than twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 defines the Exclusivity Period as twelve months commencing on the Effective Date, notwithstanding the Agreement's automatic renewals.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: There is no express service-level failure trigger. The general trigger applies only to a material breach that remains uncured for thirty days after Customer gives written notice, and the excerpt does not establish that Sections 1.4 or 1.8 are service levels.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligation ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly covers only HDI's failure to make the Site operational within the Section 1.6 period. It does not cover all delivery dates; other failures trigger termination only if material and uncured for thirty days after notice.

result.reason: The redline narrows the restriction to Deerskin Products and twelve months but does not provide the required automatic exit for every service-level or delivery-date failure. Its materiality, notice, and cure conditions materially narrow those triggers. It is not minimal because it fails to reach either complete position while adding a broader exit for any material failure and a no-payment-or-penalty provision. It also does not preserve the stated retention of HDI's brand right: replacing “during the term” with the twelve-month Exclusivity Period appears to shorten that right and make it end when the Exclusivity Period terminates. The launch-failure trigger is additionally awkward because the Exclusivity Period begins on an Effective Date defined by the Site already being fully operational.
